q23939.en: A load that sticks out lengthwise, up to 3/10 of the vehicle's length, must be marked with one or two square panels like the one in the picture.

explain.short: The picture shows the square panel with red and white stripes. This is exactly the panel for a load that sticks out at the back.
explain.rule: A load that sticks out at the back must always be marked with the square red-and-white striped panel (pannello quadrangolare). One panel, or two panels (one at each end) when the load covers the whole rear width.
explain.trap: 'uno o due' (one or two): one panel is enough for a narrow load; two when it covers the whole width.

sceneParams.caption: Square red-white panel = load sticking out
lines: Square panel, red and white stripes
Load sticks out at the back

q23940.en: The panel in the picture must be fitted in every case where the load sticks out at the back, even if only a little.

explain.short: Any rear overhang, even a small one, can surprise the driver behind. So the square striped panel is always required.
explain.rule: A load that sticks out at the back must always be marked with the square red-and-white striped panel (pannello quadrangolare). One panel, or two panels (one at each end) when the load covers the whole rear width.
explain.trap: 'anche se di poco' (even if only a little): there is no minimum overhang; the panel is always needed.

sceneParams.caption: Any rear overhang needs the panel
lines: Load sticks out at the back

q23941.en: The panel in the picture marks indivisible loads that stick out from the back of the vehicle.

explain.short: The square red-and-white panel marks a load that sticks out at the back. Such loads are usually long things that cannot be cut (indivisible).
explain.rule: A load that sticks out at the back must always be marked with the square red-and-white striped panel (pannello quadrangolare). One panel, or two panels (one at each end) when the load covers the whole rear width.
explain.trap: 'parte posteriore' (back): this panel is for the BACK of the load, not the side.

sceneParams.caption: Marks a load sticking out at the back
lines: It sticks out at the back
Square striped panel on its end

q23942.en: If the load sticks out lengthwise across the whole width of the back of the vehicle, there must be two panels like these, placed crosswise at the two ends of the load.

explain.short: A wide overhang must show its full width to drivers behind. So two square panels are used, one at each end.
explain.rule: A load that sticks out at the back must always be marked with the square red-and-white striped panel (pannello quadrangolare). One panel, or two panels (one at each end) when the load covers the whole rear width.
explain.trap: 'devono essere due' (must be two): a load as wide as the vehicle needs two panels, not one.

sceneParams.caption: Full-width overhang: two panels, one each end
lines: Load as wide as the vehicle

q23943.en: A load that sticks out lengthwise, up to 3/10 of the vehicle's length, must be marked with one or two panels like the one in the picture.

explain.short: The picture shows the long yellow-and-red striped panel. That panel marks the back of heavy lorries, not a load that sticks out.
explain.rule: A load that sticks out at the back must always be marked with the square red-and-white striped panel (pannello quadrangolare). One panel, or two panels (one at each end) when the load covers the whole rear width.
explain.trap: 'in figura' (in the picture): the rule is right, but the panel shown is the wrong one.

sceneParams.caption: Wrong panel: this marks heavy lorries

q23944.en: The panel in the picture marks indivisible loads that stick out at the back right.

explain.short: This panel has a blue sign with an arrow pointing down to the right. It is used for road works or work vehicles and tells you to pass on the right. It is not a load panel.
explain.rule: A load that sticks out at the back must always be marked with the square red-and-white striped panel (pannello quadrangolare). One panel, or two panels (one at each end) when the load covers the whole rear width.
explain.trap: 'segnala carichi' (marks loads): a panel with an arrow tells you where to pass; it says nothing about a load.

sceneParams.caption: Arrow panel = pass on the right, not a load
lines: Pass on the side of the arrow

q23945.en: If the load sticks out lengthwise across the whole width of the back of the vehicle, two reflective panels like the one in the picture must be fitted.

explain.short: Two panels are right for a full-width load, but the picture shows the wrong panel. The yellow panel with a red border marks a road train or articulated lorry.
explain.rule: A load that sticks out at the back must always be marked with the square red-and-white striped panel (pannello quadrangolare). One panel, or two panels (one at each end) when the load covers the whole rear width.
explain.trap: 'pannelli retroriflettenti in figura': the number two is right, the panel shown is wrong.

sceneParams.caption: Right number, wrong panel: needs red-white square

q23946.en: The orange reflective panel in the picture marks vehicles that are carrying dangerous goods.

explain.short: The orange panel with two numbers is used on vehicles that carry dangerous goods. The numbers tell rescue teams the danger and the substance.
explain.rule: Orange panel with numbers = dangerous goods. Yellow-red striped panel = back of lorries over 3.5 t. Yellow panel with red border on the trailer = road train or articulated lorry.
explain.trap: 'merci pericolose' (dangerous goods): that is exactly what the orange panel is for.

sceneParams.caption: Orange panel = dangerous goods

q23947.en: The panel in the picture makes it easier to spot, from behind, lorries with a full-load mass over 3.5 tonnes.

explain.short: The long yellow-and-red striped panel is fitted on the back of heavy lorries. It helps drivers behind see them, especially at night.
explain.rule: Orange panel with numbers = dangerous goods. Yellow-red striped panel = back of lorries over 3.5 t. Yellow panel with red border on the trailer = road train or articulated lorry.
explain.trap: 'autocarri' (lorries) over 3.5 t: this is the right vehicle and the right weight for this panel.

sceneParams.caption: Yellow-red stripes = back of a heavy lorry

q23948.en: The yellow panel in the picture, placed on the back of the trailer, identifies a road train or an articulated lorry.

explain.short: The yellow panel with a red border goes on the back of a trailer or semi-trailer. It tells you the vehicle in front is a long road train or articulated lorry.
explain.rule: Orange panel with numbers = dangerous goods. Yellow-red striped panel = back of lorries over 3.5 t. Yellow panel with red border on the trailer = road train or articulated lorry.
explain.trap: 'rimorchio' (trailer): this panel goes on the trailer, so it means a long combined vehicle.

sceneParams.caption: Yellow panel, red border = road train
lines: On the back of the trailer

q23949.en: The orange reflective panel shown in the picture is placed at the back to mark dangerous overhanging loads.

explain.short: The orange panel marks dangerous goods, not loads that stick out. Overhanging loads use the square red-and-white panel.
explain.rule: Orange panel with numbers = dangerous goods. Yellow-red striped panel = back of lorries over 3.5 t. Yellow panel with red border on the trailer = road train or articulated lorry.
explain.trap: 'carichi sporgenti' (overhanging loads): mixes up two panels; orange is for dangerous goods.

sceneParams.caption: Orange = dangerous goods, not overhanging loads

q23950.en: The panels in the picture are placed on the road to mark an obstacle.

explain.short: These yellow-and-red striped panels are fixed on the back of heavy lorries. They are not put on the road surface.
explain.rule: Orange panel with numbers = dangerous goods. Yellow-red striped panel = back of lorries over 3.5 t. Yellow panel with red border on the trailer = road train or articulated lorry.
explain.trap: 'sulla carreggiata' (on the road): these panels are on vehicles, not on the road.

sceneParams.caption: On the back of heavy lorries, not on the road
lines: Fixed on the back of lorries

q23951.en: The panel in the picture must be fitted at the back of buses with a total mass over 3.5 tonnes.

explain.short: The yellow panel with a red border is for trailers of road trains and articulated lorries. It is not used on buses.
explain.rule: Orange panel with numbers = dangerous goods. Yellow-red striped panel = back of lorries over 3.5 t. Yellow panel with red border on the trailer = road train or articulated lorry.
explain.trap: 'agli autobus' (on buses): buses do not carry these rear panels.

sceneParams.caption: Not for buses: it marks road trains

q23952.en: No vehicle may tow, or be towed by, more than one vehicle (except for exceptional transport).

explain.short: Towing is allowed only one vehicle at a time. A longer chain of vehicles is too hard to control and to see.
explain.rule: In an emergency a car may tow one broken-down vehicle (not a trailer) with a solid, well-marked link (rope, chain, cable, rigid bar). The towed car keeps its hazard lights on. Breaking the rule costs 2 points.
explain.trap: 'più di un veicolo' (more than one vehicle): the limit is one, with the only exception of special transport.

sceneParams.caption: Only one vehicle can be towed

q23953.en: A motor vehicle may tow a vehicle that is not a trailer if that vehicle can no longer move because of a breakdown or missing essential parts.

explain.short: Emergency towing is allowed when a car cannot move by itself. A breakdown or a missing essential part is exactly such a case.
explain.rule: In an emergency a car may tow one broken-down vehicle (not a trailer) with a solid, well-marked link (rope, chain, cable, rigid bar). The towed car keeps its hazard lights on. Breaking the rule costs 2 points.
explain.trap: 'per avaria' (because of a breakdown): emergency towing is only for a vehicle that cannot run.

sceneParams.caption: Broken-down car may be towed

q23954.en: Emergency towing of one vehicle by another must use a solid link, such as a rope, chain, cable or rigid bar, as long as it is properly marked.

explain.short: The link must be strong so the cars do not separate. It must also be marked so other road users can see it.
explain.rule: In an emergency a car may tow one broken-down vehicle (not a trailer) with a solid, well-marked link (rope, chain, cable, rigid bar). The towed car keeps its hazard lights on. Breaking the rule costs 2 points.
explain.trap: 'purché idoneamente segnalati' (as long as properly marked): solid AND marked, both are needed.

sceneParams.caption: Solid link, properly marked
lines: Mark it so others see it

q23955.en: Towing a broken-down vehicle in an urgent emergency must use a solid link, as long as it is properly marked so that the vehicles are clearly visible to other road users.

explain.short: A rope or bar between two cars is hard to see. It must be strong and marked, so nobody drives between the two cars.
explain.rule: In an emergency a car may tow one broken-down vehicle (not a trailer) with a solid, well-marked link (rope, chain, cable, rigid bar). The towed car keeps its hazard lights on. Breaking the rule costs 2 points.
explain.trap: 'purché idoneamente segnalato' (as long as properly marked): marking is a condition, not optional.

sceneParams.caption: Solid link, marked so others can see it

q23956.en: If, in an emergency, a driver tows another vehicle with their own without following the rules on a solid link, they lose 2 points from the licence.

explain.short: Towing with a weak link is dangerous and is punished. The penalty includes losing 2 points.
explain.rule: In an emergency a car may tow one broken-down vehicle (not a trailer) with a solid, well-marked link (rope, chain, cable, rigid bar). The towed car keeps its hazard lights on. Breaking the rule costs 2 points.
explain.trap: '2 punti' (2 points): learn the exact number; the quiz also says 4, which is wrong.

sceneParams.caption: Weak towing link: minus 2 points

q23957.en: On a motorway, a motor vehicle may tow a vehicle that is not a trailer if that vehicle can no longer move for any serious reason.

explain.short: On a motorway an ordinary car may not tow a broken-down car: only a tow truck may do it. Also, emergency towing is for a breakdown, not 'any serious reason'.
explain.rule: In an emergency a car may tow one broken-down vehicle (not a trailer) with a solid, well-marked link (rope, chain, cable, rigid bar). The towed car keeps its hazard lights on. Breaking the rule costs 2 points.
explain.trap: 'In autostrada' (on a motorway): there, towing by an ordinary car is not allowed.

sceneParams.caption: Motorway: only a tow truck may tow
lines: No towing by an ordinary car

q23958.en: Towing a broken-down vehicle in an urgent emergency must use a solid link, even if it cannot be marked.

explain.short: The link must be solid AND marked. If you cannot mark it, the tow is not allowed.
explain.rule: In an emergency a car may tow one broken-down vehicle (not a trailer) with a solid, well-marked link (rope, chain, cable, rigid bar). The towed car keeps its hazard lights on. Breaking the rule costs 2 points.
explain.trap: 'anche se non è possibile segnalarlo' (even if it cannot be marked): marking is required.

sceneParams.caption: The link must also be marked

q23959.en: While a broken-down vehicle is being towed, the towed vehicle must keep its rear lights on if there is no other proper signal.

explain.short: The towed vehicle must keep its hazard lights on. If it cannot, it shows the warning triangle at the back. Normal rear lights are not the required signal.
explain.rule: In an emergency a car may tow one broken-down vehicle (not a trailer) with a solid, well-marked link (rope, chain, cable, rigid bar). The towed car keeps its hazard lights on. Breaking the rule costs 2 points.
explain.trap: 'le luci posteriori' (rear lights): the rule asks for hazard lights, or the triangle.

sceneParams.caption: Towed car: hazard lights, or triangle

q23960.en: If, in an emergency, a driver tows another vehicle with their own without following the rules on a solid link, they lose 4 points from the licence.

explain.short: The penalty for a weak towing link is 2 points, not 4.
explain.rule: In an emergency a car may tow one broken-down vehicle (not a trailer) with a solid, well-marked link (rope, chain, cable, rigid bar). The towed car keeps its hazard lights on. Breaking the rule costs 2 points.
explain.trap: '4 punti' (4 points): the correct number is 2.

sceneParams.caption: Weak towing link: minus 2 points, not 4

q23961.en: A car driver must consider the risks on the road linked to bicycles: light vehicles, with low speeds and possible sideways wobbles.

explain.short: Bicycles are light and slow and can wobble to the side. A car driver must keep these risks in mind.
explain.rule: Bicycles are light, slow and can wobble sideways. Cyclists (especially children and older people) find it hard to judge the speed of cars, so the driver must expect mistakes and be extra careful.
explain.trap: 'velocipedi' means bicycles; the statement lists real risks, so it is right.

sceneParams.caption: Bikes are slow and can wobble: be careful

q23962.en: The driver of a car or motorcycle must also adapt their driving to the risks linked to bicycles in traffic.

explain.short: Cyclists are fragile and can move unexpectedly. Car and motorcycle drivers must change their driving when bikes are around.
explain.rule: Bicycles are light, slow and can wobble sideways. Cyclists (especially children and older people) find it hard to judge the speed of cars, so the driver must expect mistakes and be extra careful.
explain.trap: 'deve adattare' (must adapt): adapting your driving is an obligation.

sceneParams.caption: Adapt your driving near bicycles

q23963.en: A car driver must pay special attention to bicycles in traffic ridden by very young, inexperienced or elderly people.

explain.short: Very young and older cyclists may react slowly or make mistakes. Drivers must be especially careful with them.
explain.rule: Bicycles are light, slow and can wobble sideways. Cyclists (especially children and older people) find it hard to judge the speed of cars, so the driver must expect mistakes and be extra careful.
explain.trap: 'giovanissimi e inesperti o da anziani' (very young, inexperienced or elderly): these groups need extra care.

sceneParams.caption: Extra care with young and elderly cyclists

q23964.en: For a cyclist about to make a manoeuvre, it is very hard to judge how fast motor vehicles in traffic are approaching.

explain.short: From a bike it is hard to judge how fast a car is coming. So the cyclist may turn or move out when it is not safe.
explain.rule: Bicycles are light, slow and can wobble sideways. Cyclists (especially children and older people) find it hard to judge the speed of cars, so the driver must expect mistakes and be extra careful.
explain.trap: 'molto difficile valutare' (very hard to judge): this is a real limit of cyclists.

sceneParams.caption: Cyclists can't judge your speed well

q23965.en: A car driver must expect that a cyclist in the same lane, about to turn left, will find it hard to judge the speed of the car.

explain.short: A cyclist turning left may cut across your path because they misjudge your speed. Expect this and slow down.
explain.rule: Bicycles are light, slow and can wobble sideways. Cyclists (especially children and older people) find it hard to judge the speed of cars, so the driver must expect mistakes and be extra careful.
explain.trap: 'deve prevedere' (must expect): the driver must foresee the cyclist's mistake.

sceneParams.caption: Cyclist turning left: expect a misjudgement

q23966.en: A driver must be very careful near an elderly cyclist who, to look at the road behind, turns their upper body slowly and with difficulty because of old age.

explain.short: An older cyclist may not see well behind and may wobble while turning to look. Drive slowly and give space.
explain.rule: Bicycles are light, slow and can wobble sideways. Cyclists (especially children and older people) find it hard to judge the speed of cars, so the driver must expect mistakes and be extra careful.
explain.trap: 'particolare prudenza' (special care): the elderly cyclist needs extra space and patience.

sceneParams.caption: Elderly cyclist looks back slowly: give space

q23967.en: Children on bicycles in out-of-town traffic, even riding side by side, are not a risk for a car driver, because they are slow.

explain.short: Children on bikes are a big risk: they are inexperienced and can swerve. Being slow does not make them safe.
explain.rule: Bicycles are light, slow and can wobble sideways. Cyclists (especially children and older people) find it hard to judge the speed of cars, so the driver must expect mistakes and be extra careful.
explain.trap: 'non rappresenta un rischio' (is not a risk): wrong; slow does not mean safe.

sceneParams.caption: Children on bikes ARE a risk

q23968.en: Cyclists can ride in total safety in out-of-town traffic because drivers of motor vehicles are always able to foresee their falls or dangerous swerves caused by a bumpy road surface.

explain.short: Nobody can always foresee when a cyclist falls or swerves. So cyclists are never totally safe and drivers must keep a wide gap.
explain.rule: Bicycles are light, slow and can wobble sideways. Cyclists (especially children and older people) find it hard to judge the speed of cars, so the driver must expect mistakes and be extra careful.
explain.trap: 'sempre capaci' (always able): no driver can always foresee a fall.

sceneParams.caption: No one can always foresee a cyclist's fall

q23969.en: The approach speed of a car, especially on out-of-town roads, is easy to judge from a distance for a slow cyclist.

explain.short: For a cyclist it is HARD to judge how fast a car is coming, especially on fast out-of-town roads.
explain.rule: Bicycles are light, slow and can wobble sideways. Cyclists (especially children and older people) find it hard to judge the speed of cars, so the driver must expect mistakes and be extra careful.
explain.trap: 'facilmente valutabile' (easy to judge): it is the opposite, it is hard.

sceneParams.caption: Cyclists find car speed HARD to judge

q23970.en: A car driver must always remember the risk from moped riders in traffic who have little driving experience because they are young.

explain.short: Many moped riders are teenagers with little experience. A car driver must always keep this risk in mind.
explain.rule: Moped riders are often young and inexperienced; they can zig-zag, brake or turn suddenly. Expect their mistakes, judge distances carefully, keep a wide side gap and never swerve close to them.
explain.trap: 'costantemente' (always): you must keep this in mind all the time.

sceneParams.caption: Young moped riders: always be careful

q23971.en: Turning left is especially dangerous for a moped, which has to cut across the path of one or more lines of faster vehicles coming in the same direction.

explain.short: To turn left, a moped must cross in front of faster cars coming from behind. That makes the left turn very risky.
explain.rule: Moped riders are often young and inexperienced; they can zig-zag, brake or turn suddenly. Expect their mistakes, judge distances carefully, keep a wide side gap and never swerve close to them.
explain.trap: 'particolarmente pericolosa' (especially dangerous): the left turn really is the hardest manoeuvre.

sceneParams.caption: Moped turning left crosses fast traffic

q23972.en: A motor vehicle driver must carefully judge, based on their own speed, the distance to a moped rider who is about to turn.

explain.short: A moped about to turn may slow down or cross suddenly. Judge your distance and speed carefully so you can stop.
explain.rule: Moped riders are often young and inexperienced; they can zig-zag, brake or turn suddenly. Expect their mistakes, judge distances carefully, keep a wide side gap and never swerve close to them.
explain.trap: 'con prudenza' (carefully): it is a duty to judge the distance with care.

sceneParams.caption: Moped about to turn: judge the distance

q23973.en: A motor vehicle driver must foresee sudden manoeuvres by others, such as a moped zig-zagging.

explain.short: Mopeds can move suddenly or zig-zag. A good driver expects this and is ready to slow down.
explain.rule: Moped riders are often young and inexperienced; they can zig-zag, brake or turn suddenly. Expect their mistakes, judge distances carefully, keep a wide side gap and never swerve close to them.
explain.trap: 'deve prevedere' (must foresee): expecting others' mistakes is part of safe driving.

sceneParams.caption: Expect sudden moves like zig-zagging

q23974.en: A car or motorcycle driver must keep a safe side distance from cyclists or moped riders, so as not to upset their balance.

explain.short: Passing too close can make a bike or moped lose balance. Keep a wide side gap.
explain.rule: Moped riders are often young and inexperienced; they can zig-zag, brake or turn suddenly. Expect their mistakes, judge distances carefully, keep a wide side gap and never swerve close to them.
explain.trap: 'distanza di sicurezza laterale' (safe side distance): side space matters as much as front space.

sceneParams.caption: Keep a wide side gap from bikes and mopeds

q23975.en: A motor vehicle driver must avoid moving sideways, even a little, especially near moped riders or cyclists, to avoid making them fall.

explain.short: Even a small swerve toward a bike or moped can scare the rider and make them fall. Keep a straight line.
explain.rule: Moped riders are often young and inexperienced; they can zig-zag, brake or turn suddenly. Expect their mistakes, judge distances carefully, keep a wide side gap and never swerve close to them.
explain.trap: 'anche modeste' (even small): even small sideways moves are dangerous.

sceneParams.caption: Don't swerve near bikes and mopeds

q23976.en: A motor vehicle driver must follow the traffic rules but does not have to foresee the possible careless moves of a moped rider riding beside them.

explain.short: Following the rules is not enough: you must also expect other people's careless moves, especially from mopeds.
explain.rule: Moped riders are often young and inexperienced; they can zig-zag, brake or turn suddenly. Expect their mistakes, judge distances carefully, keep a wide side gap and never swerve close to them.
explain.trap: 'non è tenuto a prevedere' (does not have to foresee): wrong, you must foresee them.

sceneParams.caption: You must foresee mopeds' careless moves

q23977.en: It is easy for a motor vehicle driver to judge the distance to a moped rider who brakes sharply to turn into a poorly signed road.

explain.short: A moped braking suddenly is hard to predict. Judging the distance is difficult, so keep more space.
explain.rule: Moped riders are often young and inexperienced; they can zig-zag, brake or turn suddenly. Expect their mistakes, judge distances carefully, keep a wide side gap and never swerve close to them.
explain.trap: 'Risulta facile' (it is easy): wrong, it is hard.

sceneParams.caption: Sudden braking moped: distance is HARD to judge

q23978.en: A car driver may overtake a moped rider at high speed, while keeping within the limits, even with too little side distance.

explain.short: Passing a moped fast and close can make it lose balance. Keep a safe side gap and slow down, even if you are within the limit.
explain.rule: Moped riders are often young and inexperienced; they can zig-zag, brake or turn suddenly. Expect their mistakes, judge distances carefully, keep a wide side gap and never swerve close to them.
explain.trap: 'nonostante la scarsa distanza' (despite little side distance): never acceptable.

sceneParams.caption: Never pass a moped fast and close

q23979.en: A car driver must know the risks from very slow vehicles, such as three-wheel mopeds, especially on out-of-town roads.

explain.short: On out-of-town roads cars go fast. A very slow vehicle ahead, like a three-wheel moped, can be reached very quickly.
explain.rule: Very slow vehicles (three-wheel mopeds, farm machines) are a danger on out-of-town roads: a fast car closes the gap quickly and it is hard to judge their speed. Big speed differences reduce safety.
explain.trap: 'deve conoscere i rischi' (must know the risks): knowing them is the driver's duty.

sceneParams.caption: Slow vehicles on open roads: know the risk
lines: You reach it fast: slow down

q23980.en: For a car going fast, though within the limits, on an out-of-town road with only two lanes, a three-wheel moped is a possible danger, especially if it makes sudden moves.

explain.short: On a two-lane road there is little room. A slow three-wheel moped that moves suddenly can cause a crash with a fast car.
explain.rule: Very slow vehicles (three-wheel mopeds, farm machines) are a danger on out-of-town roads: a fast car closes the gap quickly and it is hard to judge their speed. Big speed differences reduce safety.
explain.trap: 'potenziale pericolo' (possible danger): yes, even if you respect the limits.

sceneParams.caption: Three-wheel moped on a two-lane road: danger

q23981.en: For a car driver at normal speed on an out-of-town road, it can be hard to judge the speed of a farm machine, which usually moves slowly.

explain.short: Farm machines are much slower than you expect. It is hard to judge how fast you are getting closer, so slow down early.
explain.rule: Very slow vehicles (three-wheel mopeds, farm machines) are a danger on out-of-town roads: a fast car closes the gap quickly and it is hard to judge their speed. Big speed differences reduce safety.
explain.trap: 'difficoltosa la valutazione' (hard to judge): the slow speed is easy to underestimate.

sceneParams.caption: Farm machine: speed hard to judge
lines: Hard to judge: slow down early

q23982.en: Vehicles that can reach very different speeds, especially on out-of-town roads, are a safety factor.

explain.short: Big speed differences between vehicles cause rear-end crashes and risky overtaking. They reduce safety, they do not increase it.
explain.rule: Very slow vehicles (three-wheel mopeds, farm machines) are a danger on out-of-town roads: a fast car closes the gap quickly and it is hard to judge their speed. Big speed differences reduce safety.
explain.trap: 'fattore di sicurezza' (safety factor): it is the opposite, a risk factor.

sceneParams.caption: Very different speeds = more risk

q23983.en: For a car going fast, though within the limits, especially on an out-of-town road, it is easy to judge how long it takes to reach a slow vehicle.

explain.short: When you go fast and the vehicle ahead is slow, you close the gap much faster than you think. It is hard to judge.
explain.rule: Very slow vehicles (three-wheel mopeds, farm machines) are a danger on out-of-town roads: a fast car closes the gap quickly and it is hard to judge their speed. Big speed differences reduce safety.
explain.trap: 'Risulta facile' (it is easy): wrong, it is hard.

sceneParams.caption: Closing on a slow vehicle: HARD to judge
lines: Gap closes fast: hard to judge

q23984.en: A collision between vehicles with very different masses is more dangerous.

explain.short: In a crash, the lighter vehicle takes most of the force. So big differences in mass make the crash worse.
explain.rule: A crash between vehicles of very different mass is more dangerous, above all for the lighter one. Big differences in mass and performance make roads less safe, not safer.
explain.trap: 'maggiormente pericolosa' (more dangerous): yes, for the lighter vehicle above all.

sceneParams.caption: Very different masses: worse crash

q23985.en: When driving a small car, you must consider the bigger risks of rear-end crashes or collisions with heavier cars.

explain.short: A small car is the weaker side in a crash with a heavier car. Its driver must keep this risk in mind.
explain.rule: A crash between vehicles of very different mass is more dangerous, above all for the lighter one. Big differences in mass and performance make roads less safe, not safer.
explain.trap: 'maggiori rischi' (bigger risks): the small car is the more exposed one.

sceneParams.caption: Small car: bigger risk in a crash

q23986.en: A very heavy car is, in traffic, a guarantee of safety also for other smaller and lighter vehicles.

explain.short: A heavy car can protect its own passengers, but in a crash it does more damage to lighter vehicles. It is not a guarantee of safety for others.
explain.rule: A crash between vehicles of very different mass is more dangerous, above all for the lighter one. Big differences in mass and performance make roads less safe, not safer.
explain.trap: 'anche per gli altri' (also for the others): heavy cars are more dangerous for others.

sceneParams.caption: Heavy car = more danger for small vehicles

q23987.en: Vehicles are safer in traffic the more their masses differ.

explain.short: It is the opposite: the bigger the difference in mass, the worse a crash is for the lighter vehicle.
explain.rule: A crash between vehicles of very different mass is more dangerous, above all for the lighter one. Big differences in mass and performance make roads less safe, not safer.
explain.trap: 'tanto più sicuri' (the safer): reversed; more difference means less safety.

sceneParams.caption: Bigger mass difference = less safety

q23988.en: Big differences in performance and mass between cars help road safety.

explain.short: Big differences in power and weight make crashes worse and speeds uneven. They reduce safety.
explain.rule: A crash between vehicles of very different mass is more dangerous, above all for the lighter one. Big differences in mass and performance make roads less safe, not safer.
explain.trap: 'facilitano una buona sicurezza' (help safety): it is the opposite.

sceneParams.caption: Big differences hurt road safety

q23989.en: An SUV driver must drive with the greatest care, knowing that the height and mass of the vehicle are a possible danger for pedestrians, cyclists and small cars.

explain.short: A tall, heavy SUV hits pedestrians and small cars harder and higher. Its driver must be extra careful.
explain.rule: An SUV (fuoristrada) is tall and heavy, often with strong bull bars: it is more dangerous for pedestrians, cyclists and small cars, and harder to drive in town. It does not give maximum safety to everyone.
explain.trap: 'potenziale pericolo' (possible danger): the SUV's size is a risk for others.

sceneParams.caption: SUV: big and heavy, danger for others

q23990.en: SUV drivers must consider the serious damage their vehicle's sticking-out, reinforced bumpers can cause in a crash with smaller vehicles.

explain.short: Strong, sticking-out bumpers (bull bars) do more harm to smaller vehicles and people. SUV drivers must keep this in mind.
explain.rule: An SUV (fuoristrada) is tall and heavy, often with strong bull bars: it is more dangerous for pedestrians, cyclists and small cars, and harder to drive in town. It does not give maximum safety to everyone.
explain.trap: 'gravi danni' (serious damage): reinforced bumpers increase harm to others.

sceneParams.caption: Bull bars cause serious damage

q23991.en: An SUV driver must remember that driving this vehicle is especially demanding in town and needs special care, above all in emergency manoeuvres.

explain.short: An SUV is big, heavy and tall. In narrow city streets and in sudden manoeuvres it is harder to control.
explain.rule: An SUV (fuoristrada) is tall and heavy, often with strong bull bars: it is more dangerous for pedestrians, cyclists and small cars, and harder to drive in town. It does not give maximum safety to everyone.
explain.trap: 'particolarmente impegnativa in città' (especially demanding in town): true, size matters in town.

sceneParams.caption: SUV in town: harder to drive

q23992.en: Driving an SUV, with its great mass and greater height than cars, guarantees maximum safety for its own passengers and for other road users.

explain.short: An SUV may protect its own passengers, but it is MORE dangerous for others. It does not guarantee safety for everyone.
explain.rule: An SUV (fuoristrada) is tall and heavy, often with strong bull bars: it is more dangerous for pedestrians, cyclists and small cars, and harder to drive in town. It does not give maximum safety to everyone.
explain.trap: 'per gli altri utenti' (for other road users): an SUV is a danger to them, not a protection.

sceneParams.caption: SUV is not safer for others

q23993.en: In a collision or rear-end crash, sticking-out reinforced bumpers (bull bars) make SUVs less dangerous for other vehicles.

explain.short: Bull bars are hard and stick out, so they do MORE damage to other vehicles and to people.
explain.rule: An SUV (fuoristrada) is tall and heavy, often with strong bull bars: it is more dangerous for pedestrians, cyclists and small cars, and harder to drive in town. It does not give maximum safety to everyone.
explain.trap: 'meno pericolosi' (less dangerous): reversed; bull bars make SUVs more dangerous.

sceneParams.caption: Bull bars make SUVs MORE dangerous

q23994.en: Driving an SUV is especially suitable inside built-up areas.

explain.short: In town an SUV is harder to drive and park, and more dangerous for pedestrians and cyclists. It is not especially suitable there.
explain.rule: An SUV (fuoristrada) is tall and heavy, often with strong bull bars: it is more dangerous for pedestrians, cyclists and small cars, and harder to drive in town. It does not give maximum safety to everyone.
explain.trap: 'particolarmente indicata' (especially suitable): it is the opposite, an SUV is demanding in town.

sceneParams.caption: SUV in town: demanding, not ideal

q23995.en: When driving a car, you should always assess the possible danger of industrial vehicles and buses, because their mass is much greater.

explain.short: Lorries and buses are much heavier than a car. In a crash the car suffers most, so stay alert near them.
explain.rule: Lorries, road trains, articulated lorries and buses are much heavier than a car: in a crash the car or motorcycle comes off worst. Always assess their danger, especially if they speed.
explain.trap: 'massa notevolmente maggiore' (much greater mass): that is why they are more dangerous.

sceneParams.caption: Lorries and buses: much heavier, more danger

q23996.en: A motorcycle or car driver must be able to assess the high risks from lorries, road trains or articulated lorries that do not respect speed limits.

explain.short: A heavy lorry going too fast needs a long distance to stop and hits very hard. Car and motorcycle drivers must be aware of this.
explain.rule: Lorries, road trains, articulated lorries and buses are much heavier than a car: in a crash the car or motorcycle comes off worst. Always assess their danger, especially if they speed.
explain.trap: 'alti rischi' (high risks): a speeding heavy vehicle is very dangerous.

sceneParams.caption: Speeding lorries: high risk
lines: High risk for cars and bikes

q23997.en: Lorries, road trains and articulated lorries, because of their large mass, are no greater possible risk for a car or motorcycle than any other vehicle.

explain.short: Their large mass makes them MORE dangerous for cars and motorcycles, not equally dangerous.
explain.rule: Lorries, road trains, articulated lorries and buses are much heavier than a car: in a crash the car or motorcycle comes off worst. Always assess their danger, especially if they speed.
explain.trap: 'non costituiscono... rischi maggiori' (are no greater risk): wrong, they are a greater risk.

sceneParams.caption: Heavy lorries ARE a greater risk
lines: Greater risk for the small one

q23998.en: Even though the vehicle's design gives a good field of view, while driving the driver must carefully look at the area in front and around.

explain.short: A good design does not see for you. You must still actively check the area in front and around the car.
explain.rule: Even if your car has a good field of view, look carefully all around: head rests and pillars can hide people, and a tall SUV can hide children. Adhesive films on the windscreen and front side windows are forbidden.
explain.trap: 'Nonostante' (even though): good design does not replace careful looking.

sceneParams.caption: Good visibility, but still look carefully

q23999.en: The driver's field of view can be reduced both by a head rest and by parts of the car body, which can accidentally hide other road users.

explain.short: Head rests and pillars (car body parts) create blind spots. A pedestrian or bike can hide there.
explain.rule: Even if your car has a good field of view, look carefully all around: head rests and pillars can hide people, and a tall SUV can hide children. Adhesive films on the windscreen and front side windows are forbidden.
explain.trap: 'può essere ridotto' (can be reduced): blind spots are real even in your own car.

sceneParams.caption: Head rests and pillars make blind spots

q24000.en: To allow good visibility, it is forbidden to apply adhesive films on the windscreen and front side windows of vehicles.

explain.short: Films on the windscreen and front side windows reduce what you see. So they are forbidden there.
explain.rule: Even if your car has a good field of view, look carefully all around: head rests and pillars can hide people, and a tall SUV can hide children. Adhesive films on the windscreen and front side windows are forbidden.
explain.trap: 'è vietato' (it is forbidden): a clear ban for the windscreen and front side windows.

sceneParams.caption: No films on windscreen or front side windows

q24001.en: Pedestrians, and above all children, risk being outside the field of view of an SUV driver because of the vehicle's size.

explain.short: An SUV has a high, long bonnet. A small child right in front of it can be invisible to the driver.
explain.rule: Even if your car has a good field of view, look carefully all around: head rests and pillars can hide people, and a tall SUV can hide children. Adhesive films on the windscreen and front side windows are forbidden.
explain.trap: 'rischiano di rimanere fuori' (risk being outside): yes, small people can disappear from view.

sceneParams.caption: SUV: children in front can be invisible

q24002.en: The driver may just take a quick look at the area right in front of the vehicle, because the vehicle has a good field of view by design.

explain.short: A quick look is never enough. Even with good visibility, you must check carefully around the car.
explain.rule: Even if your car has a good field of view, look carefully all around: head rests and pillars can hide people, and a tall SUV can hide children. Adhesive films on the windscreen and front side windows are forbidden.
explain.trap: 'controllo visivo affrettato' (quick look): careful checking is always required.

sceneParams.caption: A quick look is not enough

q24003.en: It is allowed to apply adhesive films on the front side windows and the windscreen, as long as they are made of removable material.

explain.short: Films on the windscreen and front side windows are forbidden, removable or not. They block your view.
explain.rule: Even if your car has a good field of view, look carefully all around: head rests and pillars can hide people, and a tall SUV can hide children. Adhesive films on the windscreen and front side windows are forbidden.
explain.trap: 'a condizione che siano di materiale rimovibile' (as long as removable): removable does not make them legal.

sceneParams.caption: Films there are forbidden, even removable

q24004.en: SUVs are so tall that the driver has good visibility of all possible low obstacles (for example, children).

explain.short: Being tall does not help to see low things close to the car. A child in front of an SUV can be hidden by the bonnet.
explain.rule: Even if your car has a good field of view, look carefully all around: head rests and pillars can hide people, and a tall SUV can hide children. Adhesive films on the windscreen and front side windows are forbidden.
explain.trap: 'adeguata visibilità' (good visibility): the height actually hides low obstacles.

sceneParams.caption: Tall SUV hides low obstacles like children
